FINDING_ID: F001  
SEVERITY: 0.95  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.90  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L5045](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5045) processes failures only for models present in `responses`. Any dispatched model that never replies is omitted from `failures`, never sent through `FailureHandler`, and never affects abort or recovery logic. That makes missing responses invisible at the main interface boundary.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `process_round()` take the expected responder set or allocation, synthesize a timeout/empty failure for any missing active model, and record it before convergence and immune logic run.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix defines the capability fingerprint as `(D_decay, v̄, A, C)` with `A = total novel verified findings` and `C = A / estimated total real findings` at [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L606](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L606). The implementation instead treats `A` as mean severity and `C` as per-round flaw-class breadth at [dynamic_management.py#L5411](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5411) and [dynamic_management.py#L5414](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5414). Role scoring is therefore operating on different semantics than the mathematical model claims.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either align code to the appendix definitions for `A` and `C`, or rename the implemented dimensions and update the appendix and role-scoring comments so traceability is honest.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: [dynamic_management.py#L827](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L827) computes redundancy targets from `len(self.models)`, but [dynamic_management.py#L805](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L805) excludes PM from admissible task execution when `K > 1`. For critical tasks, the solver can demand coverage by `K` models even though only `K-1` are legally admissible, so under-coverage is built in by construction.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute redundancy targets from the admissible active worker set, not the raw model count, and treat unmet redundancy as an explicit feasibility failure.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.85  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix’s format-yield model requires `φ_i`, rescued findings `F_rescued(i)`, and effective finding sets `F_eff(i)` at [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L154](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L154). The code has only a diagnosis stub at [dynamic_management.py#L2898](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2898), and [dynamic_management.py#L5153](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5153) never passes `response_chars` or `response_time`, so that detector is effectively blind in the main loop. Even if it fired, convergence still runs on parsed `findings` only.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass raw response size and timing into `record_model_round()`, add a re-extraction/rescue path, and feed `F_eff` into convergence and diminishing-returns calculations.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80  
DESCRIPTION: [verification_chain.py#L471](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L471) builds inclusion proofs over the current full record set only. After an epoch is sealed at [verification_chain.py#L421](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/verification_chain.py#L421), there is no API to later generate a proof against that historical epoch’s prefix root if more records have been appended. That breaks the stated “epoch inclusion” guarantee for historical epochs.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add epoch-scoped proof generation, e.g. `build_inclusion_proof(index, epoch_index)` or `record_count`, and verify against that epoch’s stored root.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: The `vocab_saturation` remediation changes the threshold `tau_vocab_growth` at [dynamic_management.py#L5583](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5583), but outcome verification at [dynamic_management.py#L3068](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3068) judges success by whether raw `vocab_growth` increased. A threshold relaxation can resolve the false positive without raising the raw metric, so this chain self-classifies successful fixes as failures.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Verify `vocab_saturation` against the predicate being remediated, e.g. `not vocab_saturated(...)`, or store a per-pathology success function instead of assuming “higher metric is better.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix defines delivery feasibility as `f_del(i) = P(|response_i| > 0 | budget_i, arch_i)` at [MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L116](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L116), but [dynamic_management.py#L1041](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1041) implements `feasibility_probability()` as a Gaussian capacity-fit check `P(task_load <= L_m)`. That is a different variable: uncertain context capacity, not non-empty delivery under architecture/budget constraints.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either rename the code to reflect what it actually computes, or implement empirical `f_del` from delivery history and use that in the formal detection path.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: The dispatch false-positive immune path cannot complete. [dynamic_management.py#L4085](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4085) requires both block history and later success history, but only blocks are recorded in [dynamic_management.py#L4982](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4982). The corresponding success hook exists only as [dynamic_management.py#L6053](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L6053) and is never called from the round pipeline.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Record “success after prior block” when a previously blocked model later completes a round successfully, and do it in the same orchestration path that records the block.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
DESCRIPTION: The self-adaptive immune layer’s bookkeeping is internally inconsistent. [dynamic_management.py#L2811](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2811) stores only the first batch of diagnoses in `_diagnoses`, then appends remediation-outcome and self-diagnosis results only to the returned list. On top of that, [dynamic_management.py#L3208](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3208) says `false_positive_rate` is “last 10 rounds” but uses an all-history detection denominator. That makes self-assessment both incomplete and increasingly biased downward over time.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Persist all emitted diagnoses into `_diagnoses` before summary metrics are computed, and window both numerator and denominator over the same recent rounds.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F010  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: The damping contract says fixes should be rate-limited per parameter, but [dynamic_management.py#L5698](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5698) keys damping to `diagnosis.detector`. That lets different detectors modify the same parameter back-to-back, and can also block unrelated adjustments from the same detector.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Resolve the target parameter before damping and throttle on that parameter key, optionally with model scope where the parameter is per-model.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
